The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 16.03.2023.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 16.03.2023 at about 5.35 p.m. when he was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-42-Q-3460, in between Kokkare Hosahalli village,-Hukunda village road,
Kokkare Hosahalli village Uyyamballi hobli, Kanakapura taluk, Ramanagara dist., at that time driver of the Bolero LGV vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-42-A-5520 by driving the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle of the petitioner, caused the accident, due to which he sustained injuries.

It is stated that he has spent huge amount for his treatment, medicine etc.,
3.
It is further stated that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was working as mason and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is not able to do his work as doing earlier.
It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the Bolero LGV bearing Reg. No. KA-42-A- 5520.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2 nd respondent being the insurer of the offending Bolero LGV are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: Inspite of memo of undertaking to file vakalath by PHV, not filed Vakalath and also not filed written statement.
On service of notice, respondent No.2 appeared before the court through his counsel and filed written statement.
5. The 2nd respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.

It has denied the age,
income and occupation of the petitioner and also the amount spent towards the medical expenses by the petitioner.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Bolero LGV bearing Reg. No.KA-42-A-5520 and the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and valid and effective driving licence held by the driver of the offending vehicle, valid permit, FC and RC as on the date of the accident.
Owner of the vehicle and the jurisdictional police have not complied section 134(C)and 158(6) of M.V. Act.
It is further contended that the accident was occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle.
The compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all other grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, this court has framed following issues :-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 16.03.2023 at about 5.35 p.m. when he was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-42-Q-3460, in between Kokkare Hosahalli village,-Hukunda village road, Kokkare Hosahalli village, Uyyamballi hobli,
Kanakapura taluk, Ramanagara dist., at that time driver of the Bolero LGV vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-42-A-5520 by driving the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle of the petitioner, caused the accident, due to which he sustained injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, from whom and how much?
3. What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 23 documents as per Ex.P1 to 23.
On the other hand, respondents have has not led their defence evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the documents.
9.

My findings on the above issues as under:-
 Issue No.1 ...

As per final order  For the following:
 REASONS 10. Issues No.1 to 3: As per the case of the petitioner, on 16.03.2023 at about 5.35 p.m. when he was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-42-Q-3460, in between Kokkare Hosahalli village,-Hukunda village road, Kokkare Hosahalli villageUyyamballi hobli, Kanakapura taluk,
Ramanagara dist., at that time driver of the Bolero LGV vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-42-A-5520 by driving the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle of the petitioner,
caused the accident, due to which he sustained injuries.

The petitioner in order to prove his case, got examined himself as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of the petition and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S,
Spot Mahazar, Seizure mahazar, IMV report, Wound certificate and Charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to 7.
11.
I have carefully examined the entire oral and documentary evidence available on record.
The incident said to have taken place on 16.03.2023 at 5.30 p.m. On the very next day wife of the petitioner namely Lalithabai has lodged the first information before police.
Ex.P3 is the spot mahazar, this document makes it clear that accident occurred in the left side of the road, and also the said road width is 12 feet, accident occurred on left side road edge.
On perusal of charge sheet and other document discloses that the driver of the Bolero LGV vehicle hit against the petitioner's vehicle from front side while petitioner was proceeding on his way.

Driver of the Bolero LGV vehicle has not taken proper care and precaution regarding the vehicles which are plying on the main road and taken his vehicle extreme right and hit against the petitioner's motorcycle.
If he had taken proper care and caution and driven the Bolero LGV vehicle in a slow manner, he could avoid the accident.

The Respondents have not led evidence to establish that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Bolero LGV vehicle and to establish that the accident occurred sole negligence of the petitioner.
12. The respondents have not raised any contention with regard to the negligence aspect.
Still the petitioner has deposed about the manner of accident.
There are no reason to distrust the evidence of petitioner.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the offending Bolero LGV bearing Reg. No. KA-42-A- 5520.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Bolero LGV bearing Reg. No. KA-42-A-5520.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.

14. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:

sentences.text: It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, he was hale and working as mason and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.

In order to prove the same, petitioner has produced Ex.P16 to Ex.P18 which are passbooks and the receipts issued by the Department of Sericulture which shows that petitioner was breeding silk worms and generating income from it.
Hence, this tribunal has considered the approximate income as Rs.18,000/- The incident occurred during the year 2023.
Considering the avocation and the year of the accident, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.18,000/- per month.
The petitioner claims that he is unable to work due to the injuries sustained to him.
The petitioner got examined the Doctor as PW.2 and got marked OPD record and x-rays at Ex.P22 and P23.
In the evidence of doctor, he has deposed that petitioner sustained following injuries:
Both bones(Tibia and Fibula) right leg with ACL(Anterior Cruciate Ligament)
avulsion fracture grade 2 open (compound) without DNVD(Distal Neuro vascular deficit),  Left leg both bone fracture without DNVD
Left hand close 1st Metacarpal base fracture
Right Closed 1st Metacarpal base fracture
Petitioner has undergone following surgeries:
Right leg CRIF(Closed reduction internal fixation) with Tibia IMIL (intra medullary interlocking) Nail and bolt.
Left leg ORIF (Open Reduction Internal Fixation) with Mippo plating on 30.03.2023
On 2nd admission on 03.05.2023, he underwent dynamization of right leg on 05.05.2023 and got discharged on 13.05.2023.

On 3rd admission, he underwent operation of exchange nailing with bone grafting on 28.09.2023 for fracture both bones of right leg with non-union of Tibia with implants insitu and got discharged on 04.10.2023.
On 4th admission on 17.10.2023, he was treated conservatively and got discharged on 30.10.2023.

On clinical examination he found that petitioner is facing difficulty in standing on both legs,
standing on affected legs, walking on plain surface and slope with support, climbing stairs, taking turns, squatting on floors, kneeling and sitting cross leg.
Petitioner walks with limping and walks with support of a walker frame.

He assessed 62.98% disability to the right lower limbs and 31.49%
whole body disability of the petitioner.
While calculating the loss of future income on account of permanent disability, the functional disability to the whole body has to be considered.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are not in dispute and the injuries sustained by him definitely will have an impact on his work.
Hence, considering the nature of the work and impact of disability on his performance, I deem it just and proper to consider 18% disability to his whole body.

Tholacha Niak vs Umesha S.H on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121573939/
5
It is contended that petitioner was aged 45 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 16.03.2023.
However, by considering the age mentioned in the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P19 Adhaar card as 01.01.1976, the petitioner was aged 47 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 47 is 13 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).

sentences.text:
Hence, petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.4,66,560/-(Rs.18,000x12x13x18/100)
towards loss of future income on account of permanent disability.

15. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The wound certificate produced at Ex.P6, discloses the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the doctor has opined that the above injuries are grievous in nature.
The Ex

Discharge Summaries of CDSIMER hospital reveals that petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital from 16.03.2023 to 30.03.2023, 03.05.2023 to 13.05.2023 26.09.2023 to 04.10.2023 and 17.10.2023 to 30.10.2023, totally for almost 47 days and underwent treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.85,000/- towards pain and sufferings.

16. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills worth Rs.1,16,043/- as per Ex.P14 and Ex.P15 are the prescriptions.
I have examined the medical bills and prescriptions.

Since the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone treatment, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.1,16,043/- and he is entitled for the same.

17. ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
As the petitioner was treated as an inpatient for a period of 47 days, certainly he might have spent amount towards conveyance, attendant charges, nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.50,000/- under this head.

18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 8 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.1,44,000/-

6 (18,000X8) under this head.

sentences.text:
19. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner was aged about 47 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
He has to suffer this discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out his remaining life.
This court has considered disability to the extent of 18% to whole body.
Considering all these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.75,000/- on this head.
20. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:

The doctor stated that the petitioner has to undergo two more surgeries for removal of implant for correction of non-union of fracture of tibia of right leg after controlling the bone infection in tibia and removal implants from tibia of left leg.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
Petitioner has to undergo surgery of removal of implant, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

21. Thus in all, the petitioner entitled for the compensation as here under:
Sl.
 Head of Compensation Amount  No.
 1. Loss of future earnings due to Rs. 4,66,560/-
 disability  2. Pain and Sufferings Rs. 85,000/-
 3.

Medical expenses Rs. 1,16,043/-
 4. Conveyance, food and Rs. 50,000/-
 nourishment, attendant  charges and other incidental  expenses.
 5. Loss of income during laid up Rs.
 period 1,44,000/-
 6. Loss of amenities in life/Life Rs. 75,000/-
 comforts and expectancy of life  7. Future medical expenses Rs. 40,000/-
 Total Rs. 9,76,603/-
Tholacha Niak vs Umesha S.H on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121573939/
7
In total, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,76,603/-.
22. Interest:
The petitioner is claiming interest @ 9% p.a. on the compensation amount.

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding future medical expenses) is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
23. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Bolero LGV bearing Reg. No.
KA-42-A-5520.
The breach of any of the policy conditions are not proved.
It is not disputed that 1st respondent is the owner and 2nd respondent is the insurer.
Hence, 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2nd respondent being the insurer shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,76,603/-(Rupees Nine lakhs seventy six thousand six hundred and three only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on Rs.9,36,603/- (excluding future expenses of Rs.40,000/-) from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the compensation amount, 60% of the award amount shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 40% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 2 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
